# When to use getJointJacobian and when to use getFrameJacobian in Pinocchio?

> **Current answer:** Call computeJointJacobians to update the cache. If the end-effector frame coincides with the joint, read the joint Jacobian; otherwise, read the frame Jacobian. Must explicitly verify WORLD, LOCAL, or LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED, and not rely solely on matrix values. The result must be cross-verified against official documentation and unit tests during version upgrades.

## Key terms

- Jacobian Matrix (雅可比矩阵)
- Coordinate Frame (坐标系)

## Problem and symptoms

- Unable to determine whether to use joint or frame Jacobian, and why they might be equal in WORLD space.
- API returns Jacobian matrix inconsistent with intuitive end-effector speed mapping.

## Environment

- Pinocchio, end-effector frame, WORLD/LOCAL/LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED reference frames.

## Priority diagnostics

- First check if computeJointJacobians is called, then verify if the end-effector frame is defined and the selected reference frame.

## Possible causes

- Mixing up cache calculation functions and retrieval functions, and confusing the Frame class with reference frames.

## Attempts

- Discuss using Talos configuration scripts to compare frames and joints in WORLD reference frame.

## Effective fixes

- Calculate all joint Jacobians; if end-effector and joint coincide, read joint Jacobian, else read frame Jacobian.

## Result

- Maintainer provides a runnable validation script and closes Issue, but further user input is needed for conceptual discussion.

## Limitations

- Equality in WORLD space depends on Pinocchio's definition of the reference frame, and cannot be directly applied to LOCAL or LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED.
